title: Grade 6 Science — Wed, May 20
description: Food: Where Does It Come From? — Day 3 of 5: Animal products and uses
subject: science

questions.question: Milk contains proteins, fats, calcium, and vitamins. The young of which animals use milk as their ONLY food initially?
options: Mammals (animals that feed their young with milk)
questions.explanation: Milk is produced by mammals to feed their young. Human babies, calves, kids (baby goats) all start life on milk alone.

questions.question: What is the food chain: Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Eagle? The Eagle is the:
questions.explanation: The eagle is at the top of this food chain — nothing eats it. It is the apex predator.

questions.question: In the food chain: Grass → Deer → Lion, the Grass is the:
questions.explanation: Green plants (grass) are producers — they make their own food via photosynthesis and are the base of every food chain.

questions.question: Why does energy decrease at each step in a food chain?
options: 90% of energy is lost as heat at each level — only 10% is passed to the next organism
questions.explanation: At each trophic level, about 90% of energy is lost as heat through metabolism. Only 10% is transferred to the next level.

questions.question: Silk is obtained from:
questions.explanation: Silk is produced by silkworms (Bombyx mori). The silkworm spins a cocoon of silk thread around itself during pupation.

questions.question: Which food comes from insects?
questions.explanation: Honey comes from bees. Lac (used for lacquerware and shellac) comes from lac insects. Both are insect products.

questions.question: Cheese is made from milk. Which microorganism is involved?
questions.explanation: Cheese-making uses specific bacteria (and sometimes moulds) to ferment milk proteins and create different textures and flavours.

questions.question: Which is a PRIMARY consumer in the food chain?
questions.explanation: A primary consumer eats producers (plants) directly. Deer eating grass = first level of animal consumption.

questions.question: Why are there usually FEWER top predators than grass-eating animals in a habitat?
options: Energy loss at each trophic level means less energy is available to support predators
questions.explanation: Because 90% of energy is lost at each food chain step, by the top predator level, very little energy remains — this can only support few individuals.

questions.question: Decomposers like mushrooms and bacteria:
options: End the food chain by breaking down dead matter and returning nutrients to soil
questions.explanation: Decomposers break down dead organisms into simple nutrients that return to the soil — completing the nutrient cycle.

questions.question: Why is cow's milk the most common dairy source in India?
options: Cows are widely domesticated, produce large quantities of milk, and thrive in Indian climate
questions.explanation: Cows are traditionally domesticated in India, produce 10-30 litres/day, and their milk is nutritionally rich — making them the primary dairy animal.

questions.question: Fish farming (aquaculture) is growing because:
options: Wild fish stocks are declining — fish farming provides sustainable protein without overfishing oceans
questions.explanation: Overfishing has depleted wild fish populations. Aquaculture (controlled fish farming) provides sustainable seafood without exhausting natural stocks.

questions.question: Eggs are a complete protein food because:
options: They contain all essential amino acids that the human body cannot make itself
questions.explanation: Eggs contain all 9 essential amino acids in good proportions — making them a 'complete protein' source (similar to meat and fish).

questions.question: What makes legumes (dal, beans, peas) special as a plant food?
options: They are one of the few plant foods with high protein content
They can replace water in the diet
questions.explanation: Legumes contain 20-25% protein — much higher than most plant foods. They are called 'poor man's meat' in many cultures.

questions.question: A food web differs from a food chain because:
options: A food web has only one path
A food web shows many interconnected feeding relationships between multiple organisms
A food web has no producers
A food web only has plants
questions.explanation: A food chain is one linear path (A→B→C). A food web is multiple overlapping food chains — showing that most animals eat different things.
